title: Qantas Closes Reward Ticketing Escalations Inbox
body:
Australian Frequent Flyer
Australian Frequent Flyer - Tips, Tricks and Chat for Australian Frequent Flyers
Qantas has decommissioned the inbox that provided a lifeline to customers impacted by Classic Reward ticketing failures. Photo: Matt Graham.
Qantas has quietly shut down the Reward Ticketing Escalations inbox that Australian Frequent Flyer helped to establish .
Qantas originally launched this service in January 2023 to address complaints from frequent flyers about systemic Classic Flight Reward ticketing failures.
Why the inbox existed in the first place
In the months and years leading up to January 2023, countless Qantas Frequent Flyer members had redeemed their points for flights on partner airlines – only to later find that their flights had been cancelled without their knowledge. This was happening because Qantas was failing to issue those tickets (or reissue when required) before the partner airline’s ticketing deadline.
Many people only discovered there was a problem after turning up at the airport and being unable to check in, through no fault of their own.
At the time, many Qantas Frequent Flyer members who were aware of these ticketing issues were also struggling to get in contact with a competent Qantas agent in a timely manner.
To make matters worse, back in 2022, some poorly-trained contact centre agents were even inadvertently cancelling reward bookings when a customer would call to request a simple change. So, simply getting in touch with someone at Qantas was no guarantee of a resolution either.
This clearly wasn’t acceptable and is what led to Qantas setting up the original Reward Ticketing Escalations inbox. The idea was that Qantas Frequent Flyer members who needed prompt assistance specifically with Classic Reward ticketing or re-ticketing could email rewardticketingescalations@qantas.com.au.
We understand that this inbox was monitored by a dedicated team during Australian business hours. Many AFF members successfully used it to resolve ticketing problems with minimal hassle.
The team monitoring the inbox would also proactively monitor for Classic Reward bookings that needed to be manually ticketed (for example, because automatic ticketing had failed or because of a change to the booking that required the ticket to be re-issued).
The email inbox is no longer monitored
At some point earlier this year, Qantas decided to decommission its Reward Ticketing Escalations inbox. The airline didn’t tell anyone, so people have still been sending emails to this address – but have been getting an automatic reply that the inbox is no longer monitored.
After Australian Frequent Flyer got in touch with Qantas, the airline confirmed to us that it retired the Reward Ticketing Escalations inbox due to “low usage”.
I personally find this disappointing because we are still seeing regular reports on the AFF forum of ticketing issues relating to Qantas Classic Reward bookings. Here are a few recent examples:
Hi everyone, looking for some advice on what to do with my RTW booking which hasn’t been ticketed. I called up about 2 hours ago to add some flights but never received the e-ticket confirmation and RJ manage booking website isn’t showing any e-ticket either.
I tried contacting rewardticketingescalations@qantas.com.au only to get a response that the email has been decommissioned and is no longer monitored.
I have a couple Cathay flights which sounds like they can be an issue if not ticketed within a couple hours. I tried calling 131313 but they basically said it’ll take 24 hours and just wait. So frustrating as I know in 24 hours it’ll be even harder to get them to fix it!
happyalligator on the AFF forum , 2 October 2026
I have just had an auto cancel happen to me that I had no idea about. I just happened to think I might check our seats on a flight that had been changed from Finnair to Qatar and nothing would come up under the Booking Reference. I called and spoke to somebody for an hour who told me she would e mail Qatar and I should hear back in 3-5 days. Day 5 I have called back and they still have no answer for me. I need these flights reinstated. I am so angry and there seems no one who cares or can help !!!!
KjKylie on the AFF forum , 23 October 2026
I got that auto email reply saying the email has been decommissioned and not monitored and asked to call 13 13 13. My booking for MU flight, domestic flight within China was cancelled within 24 hours after I made the booking. I could complete the booking via Qantas website and I could see the payment transaction in my credit card but was told in an email the next morning that there was an issue with payment. I was waiting for the itinerary and eticket which never came..
flyerzz on the AFF forum , 27 October 2026
I had one of these the other day on an AA flight PHL to DFW, had an email in august that there had been a schedule change and id receive a new eticket, but eticket never came and i didnt pick up on it (im usually pretty onto it given i have been burnt a couple of times in the past). Went to check in online the day before flight and got the dreaded unable to check in notice. After chatting with AA realised that it hadnt been ticketed following the schedule change. Had to call QF who to be fair managed to get it sorted and ticketed within 15 mins. I am WP so got the priority line, not sure it would have been quite so well handled otherwise…
jimmy hutspah on the AFF forum , 9 November 2026
A Qantas Frequent Flyer was recently caught out when Qantas failed to ticket their Classic Reward booking on American Airlines. Photo: Adobe Stock.
Another AFF member recently had all sorts of problems trying to change a Oneworld Classic Flight Reward booking over the phone. It took them over 10 hours worth of phone calls to resolve issues that the Reward Ticketing Escalations inbox likely could have handled.
All resolved and eticket issued now!! More than 10 hours on the phone over multiple days, some ridiculous reasons why my ticket was invalid including: Not permitted to fly Nth America-South America and then back to Nth America, Transits through airports not valid if changing airlines, No Qantas flights included in itinerary plus all of the more normal ones such as mileage, stopovers vs transits etc
I tried both emailing and calling the rewards escalations team and as noted by a poster a while back, this seem seems to have been disbanded which is a real loss as it now seems we don’t really have a way of escalating issues past the call centres.
nickfromeastryde on the AFF forum , 7 November 2026
Was this the right call?
Australian Frequent Flyer understands that the number of people emailing the Reward Ticketing Escalations inbox had dropped considerably since 2023. So, on the surface, it makes sense why someone at Qantas decided this admittedly niche service was no longer needed.
A key reason for the drop in usage could be that it’s now much easier and quicker to get in touch with a regular Qantas contact centre agent, compared to the post-COVID period that led to the creation of the inbox. Qantas has also since improved its app and introduced new digital contact channels.
The general contact centre agents, overall, are also now better trained to deal with things like Classic Reward ticketing.
But playing devil’s advocate, one could also argue that usage was low because that dedicated team was effective. As well as reacting to customer requests, this team would proactively monitor Classic Reward bookings that might need prompt ticketing. This would help to ensure that partner airlines wouldn’t automatically cancel flights, due to Qantas’ failure to ticket the bookings in time, in the first place.
I’m sure Qantas would never say: “Well, we haven’t had any aircraft accidents for a while, therefore we don’t need our aircraft maintenance engineers anymore”.
Besides, if usage was indeed low, and the team wasn’t just working exclusively on monitoring that inbox, then keeping that lifeline around – which …
